# Story 67 — Agent: my own tickets are one click away (Story: CRM-93)

## Prerequisites

- **TICKETS-2-WEB (the ticket queue) completed** — this story extends `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx` and its hook `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketQueue.ts`; both must already exist and keep filters in the URL. Verified present at `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx` and `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketQueue.ts:44` (`KEYS = ['status', 'priority', 'categoryId', 'assigneeId']`).
- **No API work.** `GET /tickets?assigneeId=<id>` already exists and is what this story uses. Do not touch anything under `api/`.

---

## Story Goal

A signed-in agent can narrow the ticket queue to the tickets assigned to them **in one click**, without typing their own id. Concretely:

1. The queue page shows a **"My tickets"** action, visible to staff.
2. Clicking it sets `assigneeId=<my id>` in the URL search params and re-runs the same queue request.
3. The result is **the same queue**: same rows, same paging, same words — just filtered. Not a new route, not a new screen, not a new hook.
4. The URL carries the filter, so the view is a link a colleague can open and one the back button restores. This is already how `useSearchParams` treats the other three filters.
5. Every new visible string comes from `en.ts` **and** `ar.ts` in the same edit (BR-6). Nothing hard-coded in JSX.

Explicitly **not in scope**: any change under `api/`; any second "my tickets" screen for staff; any change to the customer-facing `/portal/my-tickets` page.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** the queue's assignee filter is a `Select`. Setting it to the current agent means picking one's own name out of a list — which is exactly what the criterion refuses.
- **New behaviour:** a dedicated one-click **"My tickets"** control that sets `assigneeId` to `me.id` without any typing or picking; the same control (or a companion "Show all") clears that value.
- **Same queue.** No new route, no new hook, no separate screen for staff — that would put the same rows in two places.

### 2 — Wire the one-click action into `TicketQueuePage.tsx`

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx`

Changes:

1. Import `useMe` from `../../shared/session/use-me` and call it at the top of `TicketQueuePage`:
   ```ts
   const { me, isStaff } = useMe();
   ```
2. Locate the filter bar (the same block that renders the status/priority/categoryId/assigneeId `Select`s around lines 280–348). Add a new button **inside the same filter bar** — this is one more control on the queue, not a new section:
   - When `isStaff === true` and `me` is present, render a `Button` labelled `t.ticketQueue.myTickets`.
   - The button's `onClick` calls `apply({ ...filters, assigneeId: me.id })` — reuse the hook's existing `apply`; do not introduce a second setter.
   - When `filters.assigneeId === me?.id`, render the button in a pressed/active state (`aria-pressed="true"`) and swap its label to `t.ticketQueue.showAll`; its `onClick` then calls `apply({ ...filters, assigneeId: undefined })` so the assignee filter is removed from the URL. (Removing the key is what `apply` does when a value is falsy — see `useTicketQueue.ts:77`.)
   - When `isStaff === undefined` (loading) or `false` (customer somehow reaching this page), do **not** render the button. A customer should not see it, and drawing a control that will later disappear is worse than drawing nothing.
3. Do **not** change the existing assignee `Select`. It stays as-is so the same URL value round-trips through both controls.
4. Do **not** create any new file, route, or hook. The route in `web/src/app/routes.tsx` is unchanged.

**Route wiring reminder.** A route only its author can navigate to is a route that does not exist — but here there is no new route; the "My tickets" button lives on the queue that agents already reach from the desk shell.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **`useMe()` still loading.** `isStaff === undefined`. Trigger: first render before `/me` answers. Expected: button is not rendered (see `use-me.ts:42–47` comment). Enforced where the component gates on `isStaff === true`.
- **Customer somehow on the page.** Trigger: a customer types the queue URL. Expected: the button is not drawn; the API refuses the request regardless (SC-2). Enforced by the same `isStaff === true` gate.
- **Agent already filtered to themselves and clicks the button again.** Trigger: `filters.assigneeId === me.id`. Expected: the button reads `t.ticketQueue.showAll` and its click removes `assigneeId` from the URL, leaving other filters intact.
- **Other filters set.** Trigger: agent has `status=open&priority=high` and clicks "My tickets". Expected: `apply({ ...filters, assigneeId: me.id })` preserves the other three keys and resets `offset` to 0 (see `useTicketQueue.ts:78–80`).
- **Back button after clicking.** Trigger: agent clicks "My tickets", then presses back. Expected: URL loses `assigneeId`, `useSearchParams` re-derives filters, request re-runs. This is already how the URL-as-state design works; no code needed.
- **Link shared with a colleague.** Trigger: colleague opens the URL. Expected: same rows for anyone with permission to see them (the id is the *agent's* id, not the viewer's). This is the criterion's "sendable link" and requires nothing extra.
- **`assigneeId === 'none'` (UNASSIGNED) already selected.** Trigger: agent picked "unassigned" in the `Select`, then clicks "My tickets". Expected: `assigneeId` overwrites to `me.id`; `'none'` is not preserved. Enforced by `apply({ ...filters, assigneeId: me.id })` shallow-merge order.
- **Missing `me.id`.** Trigger: `useMe()` returned an error. Expected: button is not rendered because `isStaff` is `undefined` in that state; no click path exists.
- **BR-6 leak.** Trigger: someone types the label directly in JSX. Expected: `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` fails in CI. Do not add fallbacks like `t.ticketQueue.myTickets ?? 'My tickets'`.

## Review note

The plan was right and small, which is what this story is: one more value for a
filter that already exists, in a hook that already puts it in the address.
Nothing to correct in it.

Two things it could not have known, both found by the tests:

1. **The active-filter summary was printing a raw id.** It read
   `draft.assigneeId` directly and rendered a UUID into a sentence a person is
   meant to read. That was invisible while the only way to set the filter was
   to pick a name from a list — the id and the name arrived together — and
   unmissable the moment one click sets it to your own. It resolves through
   `assignees.nameFor`, which the rows beside it already used.

2. **The queue's test helper separates the requests that are not the queue**,
   and its comment said "recorded separately so an assertion about what the
   queue was asked for is not reading whichever request happened to be last".
   `/me` is the third such request and the comment was written when there were
   two — so an existing test broke by asserting on a `/me` call. The helper
   learned about it; the comment now says so.

And a note on the fixture: the signed-in agent had to be added to the staff
list, because that is how the summary turns their id back into a name.
`useAssignees` reads every page, so somebody on the second page is named as
readily as somebody on the first — which is why this is a fixture detail and
not a limitation.
